main_text.l: rea non sunt ingloria in celebriaue: quemad-
modum neque quia aurum preciosius est, ar-
gentum gloria precioque vacat. Quod vero
quod melius est, bono melius est, non malo.
Qui ergo potest, virginitatis aurum retineat:
si vero non possit ituc[?], matrimonij argen-
tum recipiat. Non ergo male facit vxorem
ducens, in Domino: melius autem non du-
cens, quod ad commoditatem praesentis vi-
tae attinet. Contra hanc libertatem pugnat
qua tyrannide cum nos liberauerit Domi-
nus Deus, sit illi honor & gloria in aeter-

l.i: filiabus Aaron, & nomen eius Elizabeth. E-
rant autem iusti ambo coram Deo, ver-
rat illis proles, eo quod esset Elizabeth sterilis,

page.notes: Page begins mid-sentence (fragment); the first paragraph continues from the previous page. The woodcut initial E is read as "Erat". The heading "Lucæ 1." is partly uncertain: the numeral may be "r" or "1". Printed "pretiosio pr.tiofius" appears garbled in the scan. "celebriaue" and "ituc" are doubtful readings. Italic is taken to run across the whole paragraph from "Erat" to "sterilis,", although "Domini irreprehensibiles" may be roman. No catchword or signature visible.
